t:
(a) Establishment.—Using amounts made available under section 48102(a) of title 49, United States Code, the Administrator may establish a center of excellence to conduct research on—
        (1) human performance in the air transportation environment, including among air transportation personnel such as air traffic controllers, pilots, and technicians; and 
        (2) any other aviation human resource issue pertinent to developing and maintaining a safe and efficient air transportation system.  
    (b) Activities.—Activities conducted under this section may include the following:
        (1) Research, development, and evaluation of training programs for air traffic controllers, aviation safety inspectors, airway transportation safety specialists, and engineers. 
        (2) Research and development of best practices for recruitment of individuals into the aviation field for mission critical positions. 
        (3) Research, in consultation with other relevant Federal agencies, to develop a baseline of general aviation employment statistics and an analysis of future needs in the aviation field. 
        (4) Research and the development of a comprehensive assessment of the airframe and power plant technician certification process and its effect on employment trends. 
        (5) Evaluation of aviation maintenance technician school environments. 
        (6) Research and an assessment of the ability to develop training programs to allow for the transition of recently unemployed and highly skilled mechanics into the aviation field.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that the 'consultation' language or the center of excellence (often university-based) counts as outside participation. But the only consultation is with other Federal agencies, which is intra-government. The center just conducts research and is not consulted on any federal decision, and the section has no public comment, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue.
fable.s: Research, in consultation with other relevant Federal agencies, to develop a baseline of general aviation employment statistics and an analysis of future needs in the aviation field.

qwen_block.w: The section describes the establishment of a research center and lists its activities. The only mention of consultation is with 'other relevant Federal agencies,' which constitutes intra-governmental coordination. Since all parties involved (the Administrator and other Federal agencies) are inside the federal government, this does not meet the definition of participation involving outside parties.
qwen_block.s: (3) Research, in consultation with other relevant Federal agencies, to develop a baseline of general aviation employment statistics and an analysis of future needs in the aviation field.

opus.w: The only consultation here is with other federal agencies, and coordination within the government is not participation. The center of excellence does research rather than advising on a specific federal decision. Like Example 3, the consultation feeds research and analysis, not a policy decision, and there is no comment period, hearing, outside advisory panel, or right to sue.
opus.s: Research, in consultation with other relevant Federal agencies, to develop a baseline of general aviation employment statistics and an analysis of future needs in the aviation field.
opus.b: The tempting reading is "Yes," because the section mentions "consultation." But the consultation is only "with other relevant Federal agencies," which keeps it inside the federal government. A center of excellence (usually hosted by a university) does research. It is not a way for outsiders to weigh in on a federal decision, and setting one up is closer to a grant or research award than to consultation.

qwen_chat.w: The section mentions consultation, but it is strictly between federal entities ('the Administrator' and 'other relevant Federal agencies'). The definition explicitly excludes intra-government coordination from the scope of participation. There is no involvement of outside parties such as states, tribes, the public, or private entities in the decision-making process described.
qwen_chat.s: (3) Research, in consultation with other relevant Federal agencies, to develop a baseline of general aviation employment statistics and an analysis of future needs in the aviation field.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "consultation with other relevant Federal agencies" constitutes participation. However, the definition explicitly states that consultation or coordination *between* federal agencies or federal officials is intra-government coordination and does not count as participation. Since all actors mentioned (Administrator, Federal agencies) are inside the federal government, this is not participation.
